name: Coyutla Totonac
world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.note: SIL Mexico Totonacan page has no Coyutla-specific publications; no phonology located

new_statements.quote: En resumen, el acento principal del TOC es un sistema trocaico silábico, ya que la propiedad culminativa se establece en las unidades portadoras de acento y presenta una intensidad máxima. [...] La regla del acento primario que opera en los verbos nominales y verbos es la misma. Es una lengua que se caracteriza por tener un acento fijo, teniendo en cuenta que fonológicamente es predecible en la penúltima sílaba de la palabra (Kager, 2007). [p. 91:] Los ejemplos descritos confirman que la posición del acento del TOC no está determinada por el peso silábico, como sucedería con otras leguas totonacas [fn. 33: ... la lengua en general el acento cae siempre en la penúltima sílaba.]
new_statements.translation: In sum, the main stress of TOC [Chumatlán Totonac] is a syllabic trochaic system, since the culminative property is established on the stress-bearing units and shows maximal intensity. [...] The primary-stress rule operating in nominals and verbs is the same. It is a language characterised by fixed stress, in that it is phonologically predictable on the penultimate syllable of the word. [p. 91:] The examples confirm that the position of stress in TOC is not determined by syllable weight, as it would be in other Totonac languages [fn. 33: ... in the language in general stress always falls on the penultimate syllable.]
new_statements.citation: Montes Castañeda, Faustino. 2022. La adquisición prosódica y morfológica del verbo totonaco de Chumatlán, Veracruz. Tesis de doctorado, CIESAS (México), §2.6.1 'El acento en el TOC'.
new_statements.locator: p. 90 (PDF p. 111), end of §2.6.1; supporting: p. 91 + fn. 33 (PDF p. 112), p. 93 (§2.6.4), p. 5 (intro)
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: QUOTE: Opened (280 pp., text layer; extracted text of PDF pp. 111-112 = printed pp. 90-91). Every quoted stretch is there verbatim: p. 90 'En resumen, el acento principal del TOC es un sistema trocaico silábico, ya que la propiedad culminativa se establece en las unidades portadoras de acento y presenta una intensidad máxima.'... 'La regla del acento primario que opera en los verbos nominales y verbos es la misma. Es una lengua que se caracteriza por tener un acento fijo, teniendo en cuenta que fonológicamente es predecible en la penúltima sílaba de la palabra (Kager, 2007).'; p. 91 'Los ejemplos descritos confirman que la posición del acento del TOC no está determinada por el peso silábico…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary stress falls on the penultimate syllable of the phonological word (prefixes+root+suffixes), regardless of syllable weight or morphological make-up; it shifts rightward as suffixes are added (k-tsíːki-y vs na-k-tsiːkí-yaː-w vs na-tsiːki-yáː-tit); monosyllables are stressed; disyllables stress the first syllable. Main acoustic correlate reported: intensity.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Explicitly not analysed (p. 86: 'este estudio no explora el foco del acento secundario'; fn. 29 calls for a future acoustic study); author notes other Totonac varieties (Misantla, Huehuetla) have weight-conditioned secondary stress.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated as exceptions; examples (12b) kín-tsa̰n and (14b) ná-k-wa̰-y show stress on prefixes when penultimate. Author stresses that this fixed-penult pattern 'difiere de otras variantes' of Totonac (p. 5). Tino Antonio 2020 Table 4 independently transcribes Chumatlán [ˈʃtaː.paːn] against Mecatlán/Olintla [ʃtaː.ˈpaːn], so the neighbouring Mecatlán dialect (Glottolog coyu1235) apparently does NOT share the penult rule.
new_statements.domain_note: Domain = phonological word (verb complex incl. prefixes and suffixes; examples up to 8+ syllables, e.g. na-liː-kaxtlawa-na-ní-kan); based on perceptual marking plus two illustrative spectrograms of isolated words; adult input speech and elicited forms from Santa Ana (Lázaro Cárdenas), municipio de Chumatlán, Veracruz.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted statement describes the Totonac of Santa Ana (Lázaro Cárdenas), municipio de Chumatlán, Veracruz ('TOC' in the thesis). Chumatlán has no Glottolog languoid; the municipality borders Coyutla and Mecatlán (Mecatlán = Glottolog dialect meca1234 of coyu1235) and the author classes it as 'totonaco de la Sierra' (MacKay & Trechsel 2015), so assignment to coyu1235 rather than high1243 (tos) is geographically plausible but NOT verified (Ethnologue/SIL toc pages were unreachable). Caution: both Montes Castañeda (p. 5: penult pattern 'difiere de otras variantes') and Tino Antonio 2020 (Table 4: Mecatlán [ʃtaː.ˈpaːn] vs Chumatlán [ˈʃtaː.paːn]) indicate that neighbouring lects, including the coyu1235 dialect Mecatlán, do not share the fixed-penult rule; if cataloged under coyu1235 it should be labelled 'Chumatlán (Santa Ana) variety'. The Glottolog-listed ref (Tino Antonio 2020) is about Olintla = olin1234, a dialect of Highland Totonac high1243, and gives no placement rule.

sources.note: Section 2.6 'El acento totonaco' (pp. 85-93): Santa Ana Chumatlán Totonac (TOC) has fixed, predictable primary stress on the penultimate syllable of the phonological word (trochaic), in nouns, verbs, adjectives, adverbs, demonstratives; not weight-sensitive and not morphologically conditioned; monosyllables stressed; secondary stress explicitly left unanalysed; author says this penult pattern 'difiere de otras variantes' (p. 5).

sources.citation: Tino Antonio, Jorge. 2020. Las vocales laringizadas y su manifestación fonética en el totonaco de Olintla. Lingüística Mexicana. Nueva Época II(1): 7-30. DOI 10.62190/amla.lmne.2020.2.1.379 (the one Glottolog ref attached to coyu1235).

sources.note: About Olintla Totonac (Glottolog olin1234, a dialect of Highland Totonac high1243, not coyu1235): no stress-placement rule; only fn.3 p.13 'la palabra fonológica comprende la base, todos los afijos y los clíticos, además del acento primario (Tino, manuscrito)', p.22 stress distinguishes /quːlúʔ/ vs /ʃquːlṵ/, and remarks that Totonac variants have 'distintos patrones acentuales'. Contains stress-marked cognates from Mecatlán (a Glottolog coyu1235 dialect) and Santa Ana Chumatlán, e.g. Table 4 p.19: Mecatlán [ʃtaː.ˈpaːn] vs Chumatlán [ˈʃtaː.paːn] 'su costado' — i.e. Mecatlán final stress where…

sources.note: It is the source of Glottolog 5.3's Coyutla Totonac dialect list (Cerro Grande, Las Lomas, Mecatlán, Progreso de Zaragoza, Sabaneta) and the family overview most likely to (a) place Chumatlán/Santa Ana explicitly within Coyutla Totonac and (b) summarise primary-stress systems across Sierra varieties, settling whether fixed penult is Chumatlán-only or general to toc. Supersedes the first reader's vaguer 'Beck in press' item; no preprint on Beck's ualberta site.
